Q1: Since nobody knows which test failed, what should the implementation deliver?
Choices:
A: Reproduce only. Run the `orchestrate-poll` group 3 test slice locally against the PR #6881 head and fix the cause of any test that fails reproducibly. If nothing reproduces, make no code change and close the issue as transient.
B: Observability only. Change the shard step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` so that, after all shard logs, it prints a short summary of each failed shard: its exit code and the names of its `FAIL` tests. Future triage runs would then see the failing test in the log tail. Pin this with a contract test (e.g. in `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`). Leave the gate unchanged.
C: A + B. Try to reproduce and fix the failing test, and also add the end-of-step failure summary so the next triage is not inconclusive. (RECOMMENDED)
D: No code change. Treat it as a transient failure and close the issue, relying on a CI rerun of PR #6881.
Q2: Which branch should the fix PR target?
Choices:
A: `main` (the default for check-triage issues). The CI summary change lands there, and the PR #6881 failure is re-checked after its branch syncs with `main`. (RECOMMENDED)
B: PR #6881's head branch `ai/issue-6868`, by adding an `Integration branch: ai/issue-6868` line. Use this if the failure is a regression introduced by that PR. **Note:** a CI-step summary change (Q1:B/C) on this branch reaches `main` only when #6881 merges.
C: Split the work. The CI summary change targets `main`; any test-regression fix targets `ai/issue-6868` as a separate follow-up issue.
